scenarios.title: Telling a story in the past

items.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
I am looking for a flat.
Could I get the check, please?
We would like to pay together.
Is this the queue for boarding?

items.tr: İbranicede şimdiki zamanda "olmak" fiili yoktur — özne ve yüklem art arda söylenir.
items.en: Hebrew has no present-tense verb "to be" — the subject and predicate are simply placed next to each other: אני מורה ("I teacher" = I am a teacher).
You want to know their name.
You want to know their origin.

items.tr: Belirlilik takısı ה, isme boşluksuz doğrudan eklenir.
items.en: The definite article ה attaches directly to the front of the noun, with no space and no separate word.

items.context: יש לכם את זה במידה גדולה יותר?

items.en: You want to try the jacket.

items.target: יש לכם את זה במידה גדולה יותר?
items.tr: Bunun daha büyük bedeni var mı?
items.en: Do you have this in a bigger size?
The fitting room is over there.
Do you have this in blue?
Can I pay by credit card?

items.tr: Saat söylerken sayının dişil biçimi kullanılır çünkü "שעה" (saat) dişil bir isimdir.
items.en: Telling time uses the feminine form of the number, because שעה ("hour") is a feminine noun.
You want to know opening hours.
What time does the store open?
It opens at nine in the morning.

items.tr: "Benim" anlamı için שלי sözcüğü, ismin arkasına yerleştirilir.
items.en: To say "my [noun]", place שלי after the noun: אבא שלי ("father of-mine" = my father).
items.context: אבא שלי רופא. / ✗ שלי אבא רופא.

items.en: My mother works at a hospital.

items.tr: "Güneşli" demek için sıfat değil, יש ("var") + isim kalıbı kullanılır: יש שמש ("güneş var").
items.en: "It's sunny" is expressed with יש ("there is") + a noun, not an adjective: יש שמש ("there is sun").
items.context: יש שמש היום. / ✗ זה שמש היום.

items.tr: Bir yere gitmek belirtilirken ל ("-e/-a") öneki, yer isminin başına doğrudan eklenir.
items.en: To express a destination, the prefix ל ("to") attaches directly to the front of the place noun.
items.context: כרטיס לשדה התעופה. / ✗ כרטיס ל שדה התעופה.

items.en: You are at a bus stop.
Which bus goes to the center?
A ticket to the airport, please.
What time does the next train leave?
Where is the nearest metro station?

items.tr: Günlük konuşmada emirler genellikle gelecek zaman fiil biçimiyle ifade edilir: תתקשרו ("arayacaksınız" = "arayın").
items.en: Everyday commands are often expressed with the future-tense verb form instead of a true imperative: תתקשרו ("you will call" = "call!").

items.tr: Şimdiki zaman fiilleri, "ben" öznesinde bile konuşanın cinsiyetine göre değişir: אני קם (erkek) / אני קמה (kadın).
items.en: Present-tense verbs change ending based on the speaker's gender, even for "I": אני קם (a man says "I wake up") vs אני קמה (a woman says it).
items.context: אני קמה בשבע. / ✗ אני קם בשבע.

items.en: When do you go to bed?
I wake up at seven every day.
I go to work by bus.
In the evening I cook dinner.
I go to sleep at eleven.
On weekends I wake up late.
Telling a story in the past

items.tr: Geçmiş zamanda "ben" öznesi için fiil sonuna תי eki eklenir: הלכתי, פגשתי, שתיתי.
items.en: Hebrew past-tense "I" verbs end in תי: הלכתי (I went), פגשתי (I met), שתיתי (I drank).
What did you do after that?
Yesterday I went to the market.
Ask for the next place or step.
Excuse me, where is the station?
Say what you did not understand.
Describe what you are looking for.
Ask about the cost or condition.
I am looking for a flat.

items.target: אני אוהב את השיעור של מדעים.

items.tr: Orada domates, salatalık ve kabak yetişiyor.

items.target: סבא משקה את הצמחים כל בוקר.
items.tr: Dedem her sabah bitkilere su verir.

items.target: אני אוסף את הירקות עם סבא.
הגן של סבא הוא המקום הכי טוב.

items.tr: Bu her zaman güzel bir akşamdır.
